hypothesis: The H5 breakout entry becomes profitable after costs when its stops are sized to each stock's volatility (a multiple of the 14-day ATR, chosen by walk-forward from a small grid) and each position is sized so a stopped-out trade loses about 1% of the account.
rationale: H5's flat 4% stop was hit by ordinary noise in over half its trades. Volatility-scaled stops and risk-based sizing are standard practice. Expectation stated in advance: H5's entry showed no edge and 5-day winners underperformed afterwards in this universe, so exits alone are unlikely to create one. This tests that honestly, once.

signal.description: same entry as H5; stop and trailing distance in ATR multiples

prior_evidence: H5 (same entry, fixed 4% stop) failed: profit factor 1.01. 5-day winners underperformed afterwards here.

rule.execution: buy at next open; ATR from the signal day; hard stop intraday (gap exits at open); trailing and time exits at close

calibration.selection: each year: highest Sharpe over all earlier years, averaged with grid neighbours (favours plateaus); ties go to the middle setting

validation.universe: S&P 400 mid-caps never in the S&P 500 (current members)

decision_rule: If every walk-forward gate passes: validate ONCE on mid-caps; if that passes, freeze the chosen setting and forward-test 12 months against SPY. Any failure closes H6: no other grids, entries or selection rules on this data.
